open_points.subject: owner-session expiry sweep schedule
open_points.text: "a pass over the sessions it makes every 60 seconds from the start"
open_points.question: What is "the start", when is the first pass, and after a delayed pass are missed passes skipped, queued, or rescheduled from the delayed pass?
options: Intervals at 60, 120, ... seconds from process start, with missed passes skipped
Intervals from each session's start
Sixty seconds after the preceding pass finishes
open_points.default_guess: Run at fixed 60-second boundaries from process start and skip missed boundaries.

open_points.subject: owner request racing the expiry sweep
open_points.text: "its arrival restarts the 30 minutes" and "The pass takes the import lock and then each session's lock ... and decides under that lock"
open_points.question: If a request arrives before the idle limit but the sweep obtains the session lock after the limit, is validity decided from the arrival instant or from the order in which the request and sweep obtain the lock, and how is the arrival recorded safely against the sweep?
options: Arrival before the limit admits the request even if the sweep gets the lock first
Whichever obtains the session lock first decides
The sweep may end the session unless the request has already updated last_request under the lock
open_points.default_guess: Use the request's captured arrival instant and update last_request under the session lock before the sweep may decide.

open_points.subject: expiry noticed by an ordinary next request
open_points.text: "Registry ends it — and drops its pending confirmation and its uploaded file with it — when it notices: at the session's next request" versus A16 "An uploaded file is changed only by a holder of the import lock"
open_points.question: Must every request to a session acquire the import lock before checking expiry because it might have to drop an upload, or may an ordinary request end the session and change the upload without that lock?
options: Every owner request takes the import lock before the session lock for its expiry check
Only a request that discovers expiry escalates to the import lock and rechecks without reversing lock order
An ordinary request may drop the upload under the session lock alone
open_points.default_guess: Every owner request takes the import lock before the session lock when checking and potentially ending an expired session.

open_points.subject: accepted import clearing other sessions' uploads
open_points.text: "an accepted import, holding it, drops every session's upload" and "hold both until done" versus A13 "The requests of one owner session that change its state ... are applied one at a time ... [with] the session's one lock"
open_points.question: Does an accepted import have to take every affected session's lock before clearing its upload, or is each upload a separately import-lock-protected field that may change while another request holds that session's lock?
options: Take every affected session lock in a declared order while holding the import lock
Treat uploaded-file state as protected solely by the import lock and exempt it from A13's whole-session serialization
Clear uploads without the other session locks despite A13
open_points.default_guess: Treat uploaded-file state as protected solely by the import lock and state that exception to A13 explicitly.

open_points.subject: configuration environment-variable names
open_points.text: "The configuration is the set of environment variables whose names begin with REGISTRY_" and "It holds exactly these items and no other"
open_points.question: What exact environment-variable name corresponds to each required item, and therefore which REGISTRY_-prefixed names are accepted rather than rejected as unknown?
options: The specification fixes exact names
Each release declares the exact names
The implementation chooses the names
open_points.default_guess: Use fixed names derived directly from the items, such as REGISTRY_STORE_LOCATION and REGISTRY_BACKUP_LOCATION.

open_points.subject: configuration well-formedness
open_points.question: What makes the store location, backup location, owner credential, service tokens and backup key well formed beyond the separately stated presence, path and minimum-length checks?
options: Only the explicit checks elsewhere in A17 define well formedness
Additional syntax and encoding rules apply to every item
Each release may choose additional validation
open_points.default_guess: Treat an item as well formed exactly when it can be decoded as its expected scalar or path and passes the other explicit A17 checks.

open_points.subject: secret length measurement
open_points.text: "A secret ... is at least 32 bytes long"
open_points.question: Environment variables are text; under which encoding is their byte length measured, and are arbitrary non-ASCII or invalidly encoded values accepted?
options: Measure UTF-8 encoded bytes and require valid Unicode text
Require an ASCII encoding and measure its bytes
Decode a declared binary representation such as base64 and measure the decoded bytes
open_points.default_guess: Require ASCII secret text and measure its ASCII bytes.

open_points.subject: existing store validation at start
open_points.text: "the store must open for reading and writing and carry the store version of the running release"
open_points.question: Does starting on an existing store also run the store's integrity check or validate its schema and required invariants, and what exact corruption is sufficient to refuse startup?
options: Opening read/write and matching the version are the only startup checks
Run the same store integrity check used for backup verification
Fully validate schema and domain invariants before serving
open_points.default_guess: Run the backend integrity check and verify the release's complete schema before serving.

open_points.subject: failed startup probe cleanup
open_points.text: "A failed start leaves no file it made but a probe it could not remove, which the next start or run removes with the other temporary files"
open_points.question: Which startup step removes a probe left by an earlier failed start, how is that probe identified, and does cleanup occur during an owner-only start where no backup run will occur?
options: Every startup first removes all regular files under the backup temporary prefix
Startup removes only a uniquely named probe file
Only a later backup run removes it
open_points.default_guess: Every startup removes stale regular files under the declared backup temporary prefix before making its new probe.

open_points.subject: backup-run mutual exclusion
open_points.text: "Runs never overlap: a 03:00 that finds a run still going makes no run of its own"
open_points.question: What state or lock makes a running backup detectable and prevents overlap, especially across two Registry processes using the same store and backup location or across a restart during a run?
options: An in-process flag only, with multiple processes declared invalid deployment
A store-backed lease or lock
An exclusive lock file in the backup location
open_points.default_guess: Use an exclusive lock file in the backup location and refuse or skip a run while it is held.

open_points.subject: backup encryption and key digest
open_points.text: "Each backup is encrypted with the backup key" and "a digest of the key it was made with"
open_points.question: Which authenticated-encryption construction, nonce-generation rule, key derivation or interpretation, and digest algorithm are required, and is the readable metadata cryptographically bound to the encrypted store?
options: A specified authenticated-encryption format binds all metadata as associated data
Encryption protects only the store bytes and metadata is unauthenticated
Each release may choose an incompatible encryption and digest format
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned authenticated-encryption format with a fresh random nonce, bind all readable metadata as associated data, and record a SHA-256 digest of the key.

open_points.subject: interrupted decrypted backup-check file
open_points.text: "it decrypts it into a second temporary file" and "the next run removes what is left"
open_points.question: What removes a decrypted temporary store after a crash when Registry restarts owner-only or otherwise never reaches another backup run, and how is that plaintext copy prevented from outliving the backup retention and erasure rules?
options: Every startup removes all backup temporary files before serving
Only the next scheduled backup run removes it
The decrypted check uses no filesystem plaintext file
open_points.default_guess: Avoid a persistent plaintext file; otherwise remove every backup temporary file at every startup before serving.

open_points.subject: backup metadata used for retention and status
open_points.text: "its age is counted from that instant" and "The owner interface shows the instant of the newest kept backup whose record can be read"
open_points.question: If the unencrypted record is syntactically readable but has been altered, does Registry trust its instant, release, sequence and key digest for retention and display, or must their authenticity be verified before the file counts as kept?
options: Authenticate the record and count it only after authentication
Trust any syntactically readable record until a restore check
Cross-check only the sequence and release while leaving the instant trusted
open_points.default_guess: Count, display and age a backup only after authenticating its record against the encrypted payload.
